description: Borrow the SIMD-accelerated DFA validation technique from simdjson's UTF-8 validator to perform Base64 character validation as a streaming automaton. Maintain a vectorized state that tracks inter-character dependencies (padding rules) enabling single-pass validation without a separate error-checking branch.
mathematical_formalization: DFA states S = {NORMAL, PAD1, PAD2, DONE, ERROR}. Transition delta computed for 64 bytes simultaneously via PSHUFB classification + saturating arithmetic. Error flags reduced with movemask/OR-reduce.
analogical_connections: simdjson: UTF-8 validation uses PSHUFB to classify bytes and check transitions in parallel
Network IDS: Aho-Corasick pattern matching parallelized with SIMD
DNA sequencing: base quality validation in FASTQ using vectorized range checks
implementation_hypothesis: Compute an error accumulator register that ORs together all invalid-character flags. Only check after the entire input. For padding, use separate end-of-stream check on the last 4 bytes. Zero branches in the hot loop.
experiment_seed: Test with crafted inputs containing errors at various positions. Measure overhead of validation vs decode-only. Target: <5% throughput cost.
